articleTitle: Three different analytical methods for calculating time varying fields from lightning return stroke
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Summary form only given. Three different methods producing three different analytical expressions for calculating the electric fields from lightning are reviewed. These are general expressions applicable to any line source distribution that varies with time and are equivalent, and produce identical remote fields

articleTitle: Double-Exponential Expression of Lightning Current Waveforms
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A lightning waveform is usually defined by the rise time t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f </sub>, pulse length t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> and peak value I. In order to represent lightning current waveforms in an analytic manner, the double-exponential formula is employed to fit with the lightning current waveforms. This paper describes the relationship between the waveform parameters t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</sub>, t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>, I and the formula constants alpha, beta and A. An effective algorithm is proposed to calculate alpha, beta and A. The algorithm gives a reasonable expression for alpha, beta and A from the data points of lightning current waveforms. Numerical examples are derived from the algorithm for a few types of lightning current waveforms that are commonly used in lightning protection design. A better agreement appears between calculated and standard waveforms

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra Wideband System for In-Body Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the feasibility of an ultra wideband (UWB) system for in-body wireless communications of biomedical applications. We first designed an implanted elliptic disc dipole antenna with a UWB frequency band in a human body. We then calculated the channel characteristics for UWB signal propagation from the implanted antenna to the out-of-body using a frequency-dependent finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. Based on the in-body channel characteristics we optimized the UWB pulse shape. We then proposed a UWB system with bi-phase modulation for the in-body wireless communications, and derived the bit-error rate (BER) of the proposed system under the additive Gaussian noise environment. The results show the feasibility of the UWB system for in-body wireless communications of biomedical applications

articleTitle: Comparison of Two Stirrer Designs for a New Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of the optimized stirrer design for a reverberation chamber which is becoming popular tool within the EMC and related areas. A new and a conventional stirrers are designed and made for a reverberation chamber of dimensions of 5.8 m times 3.6 m times 3.4 m. Comparisons for these two designs are made in terms of the field uniformity and lowest usable frequency (LUF). It is apparent from the results that the new design gives much better performance for the same chamber, which is another step towards the optimization of stirrer design of a reverberation chamber

articleTitle: Near Field-Far Field Transformation for Loops Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A genetic algorithm is applied to find equivalent ideal electric and magnetic dipoles representing the radiation of an electrically large loop. Dipole parameters are determined based on near field values and used to predict far field radiation patterns. Method of moment based field strengths are used as reference values

articleTitle: Realization and Simulation of DOA estimation using MUSIC Algorithm with Uniform Circular Arrays
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: As one key technology in third generation communication, smart antenna can effectively increase system capacity and reduce co-channel interference. At same time, Node B can use smart antenna to obtain DOA information for location service. This paper expounds in detail how to obtain DOA information using MUSIC algorithm with uniform circular arrays based on theoretical analysis of receiving spatial signal by uniform circular arrays. It also evaluates numerical simulation result of MUSIC algorithm , which shows that considerable improvement in DOA estimation performance is achieved. This paper can provide detailed theoretical basis for smart antenna practical application

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Fields of Energized Conductors in Multilayer Soils
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper discusses the computation of electromagnetic fields due to energized thin-wire conductors in a horizontal multilayer soil. The computation uses a full wave solution for the Hertz vector potential caused by an electric dipole located in the soil or in the air. The soil layers can have arbitrary resistivity, permeability, permittivity, and thickness. The field generated by a linear conductor is obtained by integrating the contribution of dipoles along the conductor. The field of an arbitrary conductor network is obtained by superposition of the contribution of all the network conductors. Both energized conductors and the calculation points can be in the air or in the soil. Numerical results are shown for several examples using a four layer soil. The results obtained with the new method are in good agreement with the analytical result for a uniform soil results in the limiting case where the resistivity of all soil layers is the same

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Electromagnetic Interference Analysis in Common Corridors
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper discusses recent advances made in electromagnetic interference analysis in common corridors shared by electric transmission lines and other utilities such as railways and pipelines (victim lines). They include new advances made in analysis methods and modeling techniques. These advances enable accurate modeling of extremely long common corridors along which various parameters may change, such as soil resistivity, power line current magnitude, fault location, and victim line characteristics

articleTitle: Gap Breakdown Field Caused by Air Discharge through Hand-Held Metal Piece from Charged Human-Body
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: We measured the discharge currents due to air discharge through a hand-held metal piece from a charged human-body with respect to charge voltages below 1000 V. The gap breakdown fields were thereby estimated, which were validated from the Paschen's law and other researcher's experimental result

articleTitle: Effect of Approaching Contact Speed of Hand-Held Metal Piece on Characteristics of Discharge Current from Charged Human Body
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Characteristic measurements of contact discharge currents were made through a hand-held metal piece from a charged human-body. Effects of approaching contact speeds on discharge current parameters, such as current peaks, peak current derivatives and spark length, were statistically examined with respect to correlation coefficients for various charge voltages

articleTitle: Interference Mitigation in UWB Communications through Pulse Waveform Design
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Coexistence and compatibility is an important issue needed to be considered in ultra-wideband (UWB) impulse radio communications. To avoid interference, one of our methods is to design appropriate pulse waveform. A new pulse design method is proposed as UWB pulse shapes by using the approximate prolate spheroidal wave functions (APSWF). The APSWF pulse meets the power spectral constraint of the FCC's spectral mask. Its mathematical expression is simple and explicit. The UWB pulse waveform can be flexibly adjusted by this method when the spectral mask changed

articleTitle: Study on Corona Discharge Test under the Power Frequency Voltage of the Severe Non-uniform Electric Field Based on the UV-light Imaging Technology
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The study on corona discharge test under the power frequency voltage of the severe non-uniform electric field based on the UV-light imaging technology is conducted. The results illuminate that the corresponding relationship between the characterizing parameter of quantifying the intensity of corona discharge and the comparing parameter is accordant; the characterizing parameter can reflect the basic physical process of gas discharge; it can also distinguish each stage of gas discharge and the distribution of the characteristic variable of UV-light at each stage of corona discharge accords with the statistical regularity. The criterion of selecting the intersection of the characteristic variable of UV-light at the stage of stream discharge as the advertent range of the air interstice breakdown is proposed

articleTitle: A study on RF frequency optimization design system related to intermodulation interference
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper proposes a new design system for RF frequency optimization related to intermodulation interference. Based on the nonlinearity performance of the receiver frontend LNA, the intermodulation products could be quantificationally analyzed. Therefore, it could complement the limitation of the old prediction system which only computes the frequencies of the intermodulation products but fails to consider the powers/amplitudes of the intermodulation products. The new design system takes into account the intermodulation products which are relatively high compared to the sensitivity but fall into the nearby outside the primary receive passband. This design system is applied to solve the intermodulation interference of a source-victim problem on a space aircraft and good agreement between the computed and measured results is obtained

articleTitle: Experimental Research on EMI of PLC System of ± 500-kV HVDC Converter Station
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The power line carrier (PLC) system used in HVDC converter station is connected directly to the primary system via coupling devices, and may be interfered by the electromagnetic noise produced by valves or switch operation procedure. In this paper, the EM noise in PLC system of plusmn500-kV HVDC converter station is measured in the steady state. The transient disturbance during the switch operation procedure appearing in PLC system is also taken into account in this paper. The characteristics of EMI in PLC system are analyzed based on the experimental results

articleTitle: Lightning: Phenomenology and Parameters Important for EMC
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Phenomenology and various parameters of lightning discharges are reviewed. In particular, direct lightning current measurements on instrumented towers and currents inferred from measured electric or magnetic fields (as done in modern lightning location systems) are discussed. Properties of first and subsequent strokes are compared. The average number of strokes per flash and multiple channel terminations on ground are considered. Parameters of subsequent strokes in natural lightning are compared to their counterparts in rocket-triggered lightning

Author Keywords: number of strokes per flash multiple channel terminations

articleTitle: Waveform Design and Performance Analysis of Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Pulse Based on Iterative Algorithm
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Pulse shaping is one of key research topics in the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) between UWB devices and other wireless systems. A low-complexity pulse shaping technique using twice iterative algorithms is suggested to achieve a maximum allowable transmitted power under Federal Communications Commission (FCC) emission mask in UWB system. In addition, the performance of time hopping pulse position modulation (TH-PPM) UWB system using the proposed monocycle is analyzed under additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel. Simulation results show that the BER performance of the proposed pulse is better than that of the other conventional pulses proposed before

articleTitle: Avoiding Lipoathrophia Semicircularis in an Office Environment
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Skin areas of office workers can be exposed to electromagnetic fields exceeding levels considered safe in standards. Such levels may cause a feeling of discomfort but are not likely to cause the disorder lipoatrophia semicircularis (LS), the local disappearance of the subcutaneous fat layer, typically in the thighs. The subcutaneous fat layer is a barrier to thermal energy and this basic function is likely to be impaired by local heat imbalance over prolonged time spans, accelerated by mechanical pressure leading to lipoatrophia semicircularis. Guidelines are presented for creating a comfortable electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical environment to prevent lipoatrophia semicircularis among offices workers

articleTitle: Lightning current withstand capacity and voltage limiting characteristics of TVS
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Lightning current withstand and voltage limiting characteristics of three kinds of transient voltage suppressor (TVS) are tested with 8/20 mus impulse current generator, and the relation between related voltage and impulse peak power is analyzed. The results show that the lightning current withstand capacity is decreasing with the increase of related voltage of TVS, and the impulse peak power can not increase the lightning current withstand capacity effectively. The limiting voltage will increase and critical voltage limiting factor will decrease with related voltage of TVS. There are decentralization characteristics on limiting voltage between different TVS of the same related voltage. The suggestion for usage and checking the insulation coordination of TVS is proposed in the paper

articleTitle: The Analysis about UWB's EMI Cause to UAV System Based on Matlab/Simulink
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: To research the systems' EMC problem between UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) and UWB (ultra wide band) is very important and practical to multi-communication-system corporate working. This paper chooses a wireless channel model to research the EMI problem between UAV and UWB systems, which based on Matlab/Simulink. And it gives the simulation experimental analytical results

articleTitle: The Generation Mechanism and Analysis 0f Passive Intermodulation in Metallic Contacts
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The physical mechanism and analytical method of passive intermodulation in metallic contacts are studied. PIM interferences in metallic contacts mainly originate from contact nonlinearity. Several important nonlinear mechanisms such as electronics tunneling effects, multipactor discharge and contact mechanism are specially described. Power series analysis indicates that PIM power should vary as 3 dB/dB with the combined input power at equal amplitude two-carrier case. PIM power should vary log-linearly with the combined input power for carrier power ratio greater than 10 dB at unequal amplitude two-carrier and constant input power case; the strongest PIM for a given power is produced when the power at transmit carrier frequency closest to the IM frequency is about 3 dB higher than the other. Verification with related reference's measured data shows that the used theory is right and practical

articleTitle: Study on Location of All-Dielectric Self-Supporting Fiber-Optic Cable on High-Voltage Power Tower
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: ADSS (all-dielectric self-supporting) fiber-optic cable will be seriously damaged when it is located at the position of intensive electric field. Therefore, it is necessary to analyze the distribution of the electric field near the high-voltage power towers. By using method of moment (MoM), the electric field near some high-voltage power towers is calculated, and the location of ADSS fiber-optic cable is presented. Then the effect of the phase sequence of the transmission lines on the electrical fields is analyzed

articleTitle: An Investigation of the Source-Stirred Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Different from the conventional reverberation chamber (RC), "the source-stirred RC" has many advantages but still lacks of deep researches till now. Based on the electric field expression for its planar model, this paper firstly demonstrates the rationality of this new method from the point view of field uniformity and probability density function

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband Aperture-Coupled Circularly Polarized Stacked Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband aperture-coupled circularly polarized stacked patch antenna. With the combination usage of the aperture-coupled feed, one stacked parasitic patch and one three-stub hybrid coupler, both the impedance bandwidth and the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth have been improved considerately. The proposed antenna operating in the X band exhibits a simulated -10 dB return loss bandwidth of 37% and an AR<3dB bandwidth of 40.3%. The maximum gain is 8.4dBi.

articleTitle: The Laminating Tunable Notch Filter with Single Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, an improved laminating varactor-loaded tunable notch filter (TNF) was proposed, which adopted only one split ring resonator (SRR) as the resonance unit. This filter operates at S band and can be tuned by the control voltage on the varactor. Comparing to the former reported coplanar SRR TNF (I. Gil et al., 2004), the laminating structure is more compact and its stopband bandwidth is much narrower

articleTitle: Experimental study on emissivity measurement of 5mm blackbody
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The emissivity measurement of 5 mm microwave black is presented. Because the emissivity of microwave blackbody is close to one, namely its reflectance almost equals zero, the directivity error of directional coupler will cause that is difficult to estimate the emissivity. Hence, we use the space reflection method of moving DUT to measure reflectance of microwave blackbody. In this method, the reflectance of measurement system is equivalent to a big standing wave and the reflectance of block body is equivalent to a small standing wave. By using moving block body within half wavelength, we can separate the two stationary waves. The emissivity of black body is given by Friis formula and some calibration parameters including phase center, gain calibration value, effective area of antenna. The measurement results are presented

articleTitle: An Overview of the Development and Validation of Large Power Grid Models for Geomagnetic Storms
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In most of the studies of electromagnetic effects performed for EMC purposes, the main approach is to study the local effects on equipment, systems or even a single building. It is not usual that analytic methods try to consider the impacts on a large extended network such as a national high voltage power grid. This paper describes such an approach that has successfully modeled several large power grids in Europe, North America and Asia with respect to their response to the very low-frequency transients (time scale of seconds to minutes) due to the threat of geomagnetic storms. This paper will describe the basic modeling accomplished and the validation of the models to geomagnetic storms

articleTitle: The Four Dimensional Linear Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the review of the study on four dimensional (4D) antenna arrays, a type of antenna arrays which introduce a fourth dimension time - into conventional antenna arrays. The analytical theory and some numerical simulation results on their applications are presented

articleTitle: Study of Step and Touch Voltages in Resistive/Capacitive Ground due to Lightning Stroke
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper aims to calculate step and touch voltages around transmission line tower foot due to lightning strike to the transmission line tower top and injecting the lightning current into resistive/capacitive ground. The transmission tower foot is modeled as hemisphere electrode impeded in the ground with specific conductivity and permittivity. The step and touch voltages are calculated for different towers lengths and different ground parameters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Propagation in AC Voltage Measuring Systems of ±500-kV HVDC Converter Station
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The AC voltage measuring system is one of the most importance paths for electromagnetic interference propagation in HVDC converter station. In this paper, a wide-band simulation model is proposed to analyze the electromagnetic interference propagation in it. Experimental study is also carried out to obtain the EMI noise level in measuring system. Comparing with experimental results, the calculation results and simulation model are verified

articleTitle: EMC design in lightning protection of computer network
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Grounding design is an important design. And it is difficulty to be carried out. In the earthing concept, it is believed very simply, but in fact and in the practical application, the grounding technology is quite complex. To find some suit solutions and methods will be taken lots of time and work, the way to suit this situation but not to solve other problems. Therefore the engineers and technicians must embark in the actual construction process from the reality analyses and the solutions of the problems. The lightning protection facility which meets some disturbance questions which bring for the computer network in the lightning protection construction has been discussed in this article, and how to find the methods for these electromagnetic compatibility questions

articleTitle: Wideband aperture coupled microstrip antenna with stubs
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel wideband aperture coupled microstrip antenna is proposed. This structure uses a radiating patch with stubs and a cross microstrip feed line. The antenna was studied regarding fractional impedance bandwidth, radiation patterns and gain. The fractional impedance bandwidth is 41%, and the antenna radiation performance is good over the entire frequency range

articleTitle: Study of Lightning Stroke to Grounded and Free Horizontal Conductor
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: An electromagnetic model was constructed to study lightning leader striking distance to horizontal conductors. Two kind of horizontal conductors were investigated, which are horizontal conductor connected to ground and free standing horizontal conductor. A comparison had been done between these two cases. A case of the horizontal conductor stressed by a DC voltage was investigated.

articleTitle: Developments in the Study of Lightning Electromagnetic Effects with Applications to the Protection of Distribution Power Lines
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In the last twenty years, the widespread use of sensitive electronic devices has increased the interest on transients, in particular those caused by lightning (direct and/or indirect). The paper presents first shortly the developments in modeling the electromagnetic (indirect) effects of lightning achieved in the last 20 years of the 20 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> century. Then it discusses in more detail two important achievements of the last 2 to 3 years, namely the problem of lightning strikes on tall constructions, like telecommunication towers and the modeling of coupling to shielded cables. These developments permit today to study the reliability of the protection against lightning electromagnetic effects of medium voltage power networks, telecommunication installations and correct the EMC design of very complex configurations like for instance control and protection circuits in power network substations

articleTitle: Calculation for the Phase Center of LPDA Based on Simulated Annealing Algorithms and MOM
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: New method of simulated annealing algorithms combined with MOM used for calculation of LPDA' phase center is presented in this paper. By this method, The characteristic of phase center varies with frequency is analyzed and the fluctuated curves of phase are presented within the main lobe in E-plane and H-plane radiation patterns. It can be concluded from the good result of phase center that this method is an effective method to calculate the LPDA' phase center

articleTitle: Study on frequency spectrum of Air Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Derivation for the frequency spectrum expressions of air electrostatic discharge (ESD) electromagnetic fields was performed with postponed potential equations of radiated fields. Using electrostatic discharge simulation and measurement set-up and home-made metal semi-circle loop, the peak currents of air discharge and peak-peak voltages induced on the loop were measured, and the waveforms of them were recorded by a digital memory oscilloscope. Spectrum characteristic of air ESD was investigated with the measured data and by calculation. Amplitude and power spectrum for different discharge voltages were compared. It is shown that the energy of air ESD is dominated in the low frequencies. The spectrum research for air ESD can provide reference and guide for electrostatic prevention technology

articleTitle: Propagation of LF-MF Radio Waves over Mountain Terrains
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A method of calculation of an attenuation function of the ground wave field by means of generalized Feinberg's equation taking into account the mountain relief is considered. It is possible to calculate the electromagnetic field in the LF-MF range over extensive inhomogeneous paths with a "bad" conductivity. Predicting maps of geoelectric sections and topographical digital maps characterizing the terrain relief and different types of forests are the basis for attenuation function calculations

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Impact Evaluation of High Voltage Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper presents a comprehensive and integrated computer approach to evaluate line parameters, electromagnetic fields, scalar potentials and corona parameters associated with arbitrary configurations of parallel transmission lines and with any number and type of conductors. The electromagnetic fields and corona parameters can be computed at any location in the vicinity of the transmission lines. The corona impact of individual phases, circuits or lines can be evaluated separately. This approach is applicable to AC or DC lines as well as hybrid AC and DC lines and it takes into account the mutual impact of lines in the calculation

articleTitle: Measurement and Computation of Induced Noise Levels in Telephone Lines Due to Harmonics in Nearby Power Lines
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a real case study which includes measurement and computation of noise levels on telephone cables due to harmonics in nearby power lines. The objective of the study is to find the most efficient and economic mitigation measures to reduce the noise levels. A circuit model has been built and induced noise levels computed. Computation results are compared with the measurement data and they are in general agreement. Mitigation measures are proposed and will be examined in the second phase of the study

articleTitle: Crosstalk Analysis Between Non-Parallel Coupled Lines Connected With Vias in a 4-layer PCB
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Multi-layer PCBs are often used in compact microwave circuit design as density of PCB layout is increased. In this paper, the crosstalk between non-parallel coupled lines connected with vias in a 4-layer PCB is investigated theoretically based on the circuit-concept approach. Non-parallel coupled lines connected with vias in a 4-layer PCB are divided into three sections, which are coupled microstrip lines and upper via section, center via section, and lower via and coupled microstrip lines section, respectively. Each section is represented by ABCD matrix. By cascading these three ABCD matrices crosstalk between non-parallel coupled lines connected with vias in a 4-layer PCB is approximately calculated. The validity of this theoretical approach is verified by comparing the calculated results with the simulated ones using HFSS

articleTitle: Simulation of EMP coupling to thin lines using three-dimensional ADI-FDTD method
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the EMP coupling to thin lines is simulated using three-dimensional ADI-FDTD method. To simplify the modification of update equation near TF/SF connective boundary, the plane wave is introduced by defining a set of equivalent currents on a closed Huygen's surface. The numerical results indicate that under the illumination of EMP wave, the peak value of induced current is not linear with the length of line. When the length of line reaches certain value the induced current can be found have a maximum peak value. With the electric field intensity of 50 kVm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, the peak value of induced current can come to several ten amperes

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Split Stirrer in Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Reverberation chambers are used widely for EMC testing in industry. The design of the mechanical stirrer should be considered artistically. This paper introduces a split stirrer design, the simulation result shows the good performance of this stirrer and a prototype chamber is built according to the simulation. The critical parameters of the reverberation chamber are analyzed in detail. Four calibrations are processed to evaluate the testing repeatability and validate the performance of the split stirrer

articleTitle: Design of capacitive-coupled broadband microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The narrow bandwidth property of a microstrip antenna is one of the important reasons to restrict its wide application. A new method for designing broadband microstrip patch antenna in capacitive-coupled structures is presented in this paper. The measured results show that the antennas have an impedance bandwidth of 42% for VSWR less than 2

articleTitle: The Study of CM EMI Cancellation in Inverter Based on Compensation Principle
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Because of the special limitation to the ground capacitance in inverter, it's difficult to cancel the serious common-mode noise and the ground current for using large CM filter. In this paper a passive cancellation method for CM EMI in power electronic converter is introduced. This new technique canceling EMI just needs a compensating transformer winding and a compensating capacitor. Since the different structures of the devise result in different paths of CM noise, two EMI compensate ways were chose to compensating the main noise in inverter. This paper also discussed the factors inference the high-frequency compensation issues and give effective solutions. Simulation and experimental results approved good effects of these cancellation techniques

articleTitle: Modeling Techniques for Analyzing Electromagnetic Interference Caused by High Voltage Power Lines to Neighboring Communication Cables
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Advanced electromagnetic interference techniques and simulation methods, used to model a complex network that includes multiple interconnected transmission and distribution line systems, nearby communication cables, and buried metallic structures, are presented in this paper. The simulations have been conducted in order to analyze electromagnetic interference of the high voltage power lines on the communication cables. Several scenarios have been explored to determine the interference level and evaluate possible mitigative measures to effectively reduce the induced currents and voltages along the communication cables to safe levels

articleTitle: The Simulation of Interference between the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) System and the CDMA System based on Simulink
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: With the development of the information technology, especially the wireless communications, the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problem between systems becomes more and more important. This paper uses Simulink to analyze the interference between the UAV system and the CDMA system, besides giving some discussion on the result

articleTitle: PLC Studies in China as a Contribution to the Development of International Standards
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In the field of PLC, the standardization process on international level is progressing very slowly. The EMC Laboratory of the North China Electric Power University has received the task to develop a measurement method for the field radiated by PLC installations and a standard to be used in the future for the regulation of the PLC deployment. After a short introduction of the standardization process at international level, the paper presents measurements performed at the North China Electric Power University of radiated fields due to PLC. Comparisons of the field with various limits are shown. Finally the paper also presents a review of the regulatory situation on international level

articleTitle: Influence of Power System's Harmonic Voltage and Interphase Interference to On-line Resistive Leakage Current monitoring of MOA
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Surge arrester is an important over voltage protection equipment in substation, and the latent faults of MOA can be found by on-line resistive leakage current monitoring. However, the existence of harmonic voltages in the power system will influence the monitoring accuracy. At the same time, because of influence of location and distributing mode of MOA, the voltage of two other phases affect single MOA by interphase interference, and this will surely influence the monitoring accuracy of MOA's resistive leakage current too. In this paper, the influence is analyzed and the method to separate the resistive leakage current under the existence of harmonic voltage is analyzed

articleTitle: Primary and Secondary EMF Standards
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: EMF measurements are one of the least accurate within the metrology of physical magnitudes. While many of the latter, for instance frequency, are measured with inaccuracy below e-10, in the case of the former the inaccuracy on the level of 1 dB is as accepted as the best, but only in the case of the far field measurements and inaccuracy on the level of 3 dB, or even 6 dB in the near field measurements is very of the to be accepted. Apart from other factors limiting accuracy of the measurement one of the most important of them is inaccuracy (class) of the EMF standards applied for their calibration. The activities in the field of EMF standards are presented

articleTitle: Differences in Specifications of Field Uniformity for GTEM Cell between the Standard IEC 61000-4-3: 2002 and IEC 61000-4-20: 2003
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The standard IEC 61000-4-20:2003 includes the GTEM cell as a measurement facility for EMC emission and immunity testing. The aim of the IEC 61000-4-3:2002 standard is to establish a common reference for radiated electromagnetic fields immunity tests. This paper describes the differences in requirements of fields uniformity assessment between the above-mentioned two standards and also gives suggestions to the performance improvement of GTEM cell according to IEC61000-4-20:2003

articleTitle: A New GA Method for Array Pattern Synthesis with Null Steering
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A genetic algorithm based on double population is presented and applied to synthesize the array antenna pattern by controlling only the current amplitudes. The algorithm includes global and local population, and each population has different objective function, fitness evaluation and genetic programming. Numerical results proved that DPGA has advantages of fast convergence rate and reliability in array antenna synthesis. Compared with existing algorithms, DPGA has no limitation to the frequency of the antenna and avoids the premature convergence

articleTitle: Correlation between the field strength measurement and the absorbing clamp measurement
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In the frequency range of 30 to 300 MHz, radiated disturbances from electronic equipment are usually measured with an antenna. In contrast, disturbances of a household appliance are evaluated using an absorbing clamp attached on the mains cable. Hence, theoretical and experimental investigations are carried out on the correlation between the field strength measurement and the absorbing clamp measurement

articleTitle: Jitter Frequency Modulation – A Technique that Can Reduce EMI Noise Level of Switch Mode Power Supply Effectively
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The analysis of the theory and realization on reducing EMI with jitter frequency modulation technology is presented. EMI tests and comparison are accomplished respectively on a 60 W switch mode power supply controlled by Top249 integrated with frequency jittering function and a 2 KW high-power switch mode power supply controlled by TL494. The results prove that this technique has a remarkable effect on decrease EMI noise level

articleTitle: Rise Time Limit of Discharge Current for Air Discharge of an ESD-gun
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Using a 12-GHz digital oscilloscope, we measured discharge currents for air discharge of an ESD-gun with charge voltages below 1 kV, and demonstrated that the rise time reached the limit of measurement. Based on the Gaussian response of the oscilloscope, the rise time limit was investigated

articleTitle: Getting Material Parameters of Absorbing Structures by Genetic Evolutional Algorithm
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, genetic evolutional algorithm is used for getting material parameters of absorbing structures. Reflection coefficients are measured by system based on free-space method. For improving precision, normal distributed random variable is used in genetic evolutional algorithm. By this method, the parameters of the unknown layer can be gotten from absorbing structure effectively. This method can solve multi-values problems brought from traditional transmission line method

articleTitle: The Analysis and Design of Line Impedance Stabilization Network for an In-house Laboratory
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The analysis and design of line impedance stabilization network (LISN) is presented. The details will be described how to design and stabilize the impedance of LISN at frequency range 150 kHz to 30 MHz following CISPR 16-1 standard. The impedance response of passive components: resistor, inductor and capacitor will be measured to identify the component parasitic. The comparison of simulated and measured result will be done and analyzed. The low cost and good impedance of the response are achieved, for in-house test, comparing to CISPR standard and also with commercial LISN

articleTitle: A Compact C-Band Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) is a high power microwave (HPM) pulsed device, potentially of gigawatt power, that combines the technologies of magnetically insulated electron flow with a slow wave structure (SWS). This combination makes the tube a device capable of operating over a wide voltage range. Our concern is to design a compact experimental setup. Using the theoretical and experimental results as guides, a novel RF choke and a beam dump disk have been introduced into the MILO. In experiments, high power microwave of the TM <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode is generated from the device with a frequency range of 3.70-3.72 GHz and a power level of above 500 MW, when the diode voltage is 400-430 kV and the beam current is 30-33 kA. The experimental results are in agreement with the computation values

articleTitle: Frequency Effective Mobile Communication System
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: One of possible options to achieve good frequency efficiency in mobile communication is the OFDMA method. It provides rather good performance for the point-to-multipoint transmission in systems without considerable Doppler frequency offset. However, increasing of the used frequency band and permanent growing of the traffic make Doppler shift influence more and more critical point in radio modems design. Here a principally new method of multiple access - so called frequency bank signal (FBS) - is proposed. FBS combines the phase shift compensation used in the PAL-TV system, OFDMA principle and spread spectrum idea with Walsh functions. This method allows mitigating influence of multipath propagation and Doppler shift. The main FBS advantage is that the error probability is almost totally non-sensitive to the Doppler effect, separate signals delay and reflected signals influence. FBS signal don't need of special pilot, synchronization or equalization signals

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupling Between Two Bent Transmission Lines by a Circuit-Concept Approach
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The crosstalk of two bent transmission lines of arbitrary directions have been analyzed by a circuit concept approach. The results for the circuit concept approach, HFSS and measurements are in very good agreement. The derived equations can be expected to be easily applied them for analyzing crosstalk of a various kind of bent transmission lines in printed circuit board

articleTitle: Study on the Statistical Properties of Laser Beam Propagation Through the Turbulent Atmosphere in the Slant-path
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The extended Huygens-Fresnel principle and ITU-R atmosphere model presented in 2001 by ITU-R are utilized to studied the statistical properties of laser beam propagation through the atmosphere turbulent in the slant path. It is assumed in the analysis that phase perturbation of the waves is the dominant effect due to the atmosphere turbulence and laser beam scattering from a diffuse target, the treatment includes the effects of the turbulent atmosphere both on the laser beam as it propagates to the target and it propagates back to the receiver. The statistical function includes the mutual coherence function, covariance of irradiance, and the power spectral density are calculated and discussed in detail

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Conducted Disturbance Source in Fuel Cell Bus
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Fuel cell vehicle would cause serious EMC (electromagnetic compatibility) problems. Now the related EMC research is being focused on. Up to now, there still have been no expert EMC standards on it. So it is necessary to realize the characteristics of the disturbance source on the new type of fuel cell vehicle. This paper applied statistical methods to analyze the conducted disturbance sources on fuel cell bus in time-domain based on a quantity of experimental results. The influence of time and operation condition is analyzed. The characteristics of the EMI sources are summed up. The results would be a necessary reference for simulation and other further automotive EMC research

articleTitle: High Performance Analog & Digital Mixed-Signal and DSP Control Systems Design for Reduced EMI
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Modern high performance control applications demanded from mixed-signal and digital signal processors (DSPs) are ever increasing. As digital circuits and DSP operate at a higher rate, a considerable amount of noise and radiation degrades the system's performance and creates EMI problems that make it difficult to pass tests required to obtain certification by the EMC regulations. In this paper, we introduce some effective methods for reduced EMI of the measurement and control systems, which are power supply design, clock and phase-locked loop (PLL) isolation, decoupling techniques, digital and analog partitioning, printed circuit board (PCB) layout, and so on for meeting many challenges of mixed-signal and DSP systems design. Design guidelines for improved EMC and signal integrity are derived from the results obtained, thus, the evaluation board of the measurement and control systems is especially suitable for performing function in high definition array induction log (HDAIL)

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band PIFA with U- and Meanderline-Shaped Slots
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, a planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) with U-and meanderline-shaped slots (UM-PIFA) is introduced. The proposed PIFA is compact with single feed and single short strip. It operates at the frequency bands of 2.65 GHz for MMDS (multichannel multipoint distribution service) and 8.20 GHz for UWB (ultra wideband). This paper will describe its geometry and performance depending on several parameters

articleTitle: Complete space - time validation of a single mode stirrer reverberation chamber for immunity testing
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper gives an overview of the validation measurements in a small cubic reverberation chamber (15 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) equiped with a single mode stirrer and two TEM horns set in cross-polarization in order to enhance the unpolarized character of the stochastic fields. Frequencies of interest are between 900 MHz and 2.5 GHz. The set of results points out that what could be firstly seen as a drawback - the cubic shape - can be effectively overcome by the design quality of the stirrer. Space homogeneity, quality factor, chamber gain, stirring ratio and CDF at 900 MHz and 1800 MHz (GSM, DECT and DCS mobile radio systems) are presented and critically commented

articleTitle: The Study of Reducing EMI in Power Electronic Converters Using SSFM Control Techniques
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper dissertates that using spread spectrum frequency modulation (SSFM) control techniques for carrier will reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI) in power electronic converters. It demonstrates that the SSFM control can lower the peak amplitude at carrier and its harmonic frequencies effectively. Several SSFM effects for sinusoidal carrier and PWM carrier with different periodic signals are discussed. It also presents that SSFM with periodic signal can control the bandwidth so that filters can be designed expediently. Finally, the paper probes into the problem of restraining EMI at some certain frequency using SSFM control techniques

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Resolving Problem of Tolerance in Radar Signal Sorting
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Firstly, the problem of tolerance of radar signal sorting is analyzed in modern electronic warfare that faces even more complex and dense pulses environments. It has become a vital factor to reduce the efficiency of sorting of the conventional multi-parameters signal sorting system. Secondly, a novel radar signal sorting method is to be presented based on support vector clustering (SVC) and cascade coupling according to the idea of statistics learning theory. It prevented tolerance from affecting radar signal sorting. The simulation experiment shows that this method is efficient on high dense pulses and complex signals environments

articleTitle: Evaluation of UWB Interference to the 3rd Generation Communication Systems
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A three-dimensional integral model of hollow spherical distribution is proposed to evaluate the UWB interference effect on 3G systems under different UWB emission power limit regulations of FCC, ETSI, and Japan respectively. The relationship between UWB device density and the link budget margin of 3G systems is established to measure the UWB interference effect on 3G systems

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: The European Directive to Protect Workers in Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The Directive 2004/40/CE to protect workers in electromagnetic fields was published for Europe. The member states have to implement the directive in their legal codes for workers within four years. In the mean time many obligations have already to be fulfilled in industry. An overview is given of the best way to cope with the new Directive in particular when using high frequency and microwave power equipment

articleTitle: Research of Electro-Thermal Memory Effect of RF Power Amplifier based on LDMOS FET
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper clarifies the relation of junction temperature of FET and its dissipated power and the essential causation of electro-thermal memory effects due to theoretical analysis, taking the LDMOS RF power amplifier as an example. The impact of electro-thermal memory effect for the performance of RF power amplifier is analyzed by Agilent ADS simulation and measurement. And the method to reduce memory effect is educed on this basis

articleTitle: The Interaction between PIFA for Bluetooth applications and a High-Fidelity Human Body Model
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The SAR distribution in a high-fidelity human body model caused by 2.4 GHz band planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) for Bluetooth application has been studied by sub-grid finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The investigated situation was a user, who was simulated by a high-fidelity human body model, wearing Bluetooth device right before his chest. The results indicated that the highest SAR areas were the body surface near the antenna. The ten-gram averaged peak SAR of lung, small intestine and blood is comparatively high. The peak SAR levels will be lower than the safety limits for an antenna output power below 80 mW

articleTitle: Automatic Target Recognition Based On Sequences of High Resolution Radar Range-Profiles
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the potential for identifying airborne or ground targets using high resolution radar (HRR) range-profiles, in conjunction with a correlator, is investigated. One type of filter is described which maximizes the expected value of certain correlation peaks. The effectiveness of the filter was investigated in an identification experiment using a dataset of correlation filters from simulated radar range profiles for 4 different ground targets. The simulated range-profiles are produced by graphical electromagnetic computing (GRECO) method. The result suggests that reliable identification is possible provided target aspect information is used and identifications are based on multiple filters

articleTitle: EMC Assessment on Power Frequency Radiation in High-Rise Building
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Substations, electrical rooms and high current busway risers are placed in secured vaults, and commonly located within the buildings, where a high level of magnetic field radiation is generated; this situation has raise the concern on human safety issue particularly for high-rise buildings. In this paper, an assessment of magnetic field radiations at power frequency inside a high-rise building in Hong Kong is described, and the measured magnetic field is referenced to the safety limits stated in ICNIRP guideline

articleTitle: Pattern Synthesis of Sparse Phased Array Antenna Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: One method of pattern synthesis for sparse phased array antenna using genetic algorithms is introduced. We start with an introduction to genetic algorithms and then consider the problem of finding the best amplitude layout of elements in sparse arrays

articleTitle: A Novel Bandpass Filter Using A Dual-Mode Square Patch Resonator with Combined CPW and Microstrip Input/Output
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel bandpass filter using a dual-mode square-patch resonator is proposed in this letter. The input and the output of the filter are constructed on a coplanar-waveguide (CPW) and a microstrip line, respectively. Therefore, a transition of CPW/microstrip may be simultaneously realized by using the filter. The filter has been investigated numerically and experimentally. Measured results show that the minimum insertion loss in the passband of the filter is about 2.1 dB and its out-of-band rejection level is below -23 dB

articleTitle: Some advancements in antenna near/far field calculation for EMC prediction
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Several novel approaches are summarized, which are from our EMC project practices for recent years. These include: (1) a universal near/far field algorithm; (2) a deductive method for near/far field estimate; (3) element technique combined with GTD approaches to predict near/far field. Some examples are shown to support these approaches. They may be widely used in the antenna analysis and EMC prediction

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Capability Design of the High-Voltage Switch Electronic Power Conditioner in the Microwave Power Module
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a high-voltage switch electronic power conditioner (EPC) configuration which be used for the microwave power module (MPM). The detailed electromagnetic capability analysis and simulation waveforms are included in this paper about high-voltage switch electronic power conditioner in the microwave power module (MPM). The electromagnetic capability analysis presented here is important to make sure the MPM have the high stability and the high reliability

Author Keywords: the high-voltage switch electronic power conditioner

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Characteristics of Metal Wire-Dielectric Composites
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Based on the electromagnetic scattering theory of dielectric wire and effective medium theory, the effective dielectric constant in the simple-cubic lattice of metal wire is derived. Numerical result reveals that effective dielectric constant become negative at frequency below some frequency, which in the case of a strong skin effect, is determined by the crystal structure only. The reflection characteristics of this material then are analyzed here in the frequency spectrum where the negative effective dielectric constant occurs

articleTitle: Research on 2-Channel Outdoor Radar Target Scattering Measurement System
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A 2-channel system based on pulse-to-pulse frequency shifting technique was designed and realized for outdoor radar target scattering measurement. The system can perform radar-cross section (RCS) measurement simultaneously on two fixed frequency bands, and test 2-dimension imaging cooperated with a rotation platform. The principle of the pulse-to-pulse frequency shifting is summarized, the design is presented and an actual result is given

articleTitle: Intrinsic Characterization of Human Metal ESD: Current, Electromagnetic Field and Displacement Current
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper advances an electrostatic discharge displacement current (ESDDC) which will "flow" through the space to all the victim devices on the EUT when discharge occurs and the ESDDC contributes to the failure of the equipment besides the discharge current and the electromagnetic field radiated from the ESD. Experiments were performed to test the ESDDC. The results show that the ESDDC is one of the major characters of the electrostatic discharge

articleTitle: Study on the through-the-wall Propagation Characteristics of UWB Signal Waveform Distortion
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Investigating the propagation properties of Ultra-wideband (UWB) is the essential topics in UWB channel theory. Based on Fourier transform theory, the distortion of various UWB impulse waveforms with indoor refraction is studied in this paper. A comparison of Fourier transform results with time-domain accurate results shows good agreements. Finally, Properties of pulse waveform distortion is analyzed.

articleTitle: Study on UWB and HPM Propagation in Circular Tunnel Using BOR-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, a body of revolution finite difference time domain (BOR-FDTD) is introduced. The propagation of the high power microwave (HPM) and ultra wide band (UWB) electromagnetic pulse in circular tunnel is analyzed for the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> modes with BOR-FDTD. The numerical and experimental results showed good agreement

articleTitle: Calculation of Lightning Induced Voltages on a Line over Finitely Conducting Ground
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the lightning generated electromagnetic fields over lossy ground are calculated using the FDTD method, then the calculated horizontal electrical field is put into the discretized Agrawal coupling equations for the calculation of the induced voltages on an overhead line. And finally comparison of the computed results with literature shows the validity of the proposed method

articleTitle: Hypothesis of Hornets Biological THF RADAR for Detection Tracking and Communication DF
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The hypothesis of a biological tremendous high frequency (THF) sophisticated radio detection and ranging (RADAR) for detection and tracking assisting hornet flight is analyzed and developed. The results of the developments described in this paper enhance the validity of our hypothesis. They may also provide tools to improve real tracking and direction finding DF systems performances and to develop specific applications to these novel hornet properties especially in the yet not sufficiently explored submillimeter wavelength bands

articleTitle: Calculation of Residual Flux Based on Preisach Model and Entering Phase control of transformer to eliminate Inrush Current
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: When transformer enters into power system without load form last cutting off, which because of action of protective device in answer to system fault and changes of system framework structure, the residual flux of ferromagnetic-core is of no randomicity. Firstly on the basis of time-character of ferromagnetic material analysis, combined with Preisach model, a way to calculate residual flux is proposed in this paper. After this, an expression between residual flux and entering-phase is educed to eliminate inrush current in single phase transformer, then its rationality has been testified by an EMTP test. Meanwhile, the simulation has discovered some rules between residual flux and the range of entering-phase at a given overshoot limit of inrush current. Finally these rules have been used to propose a control tactic about entering phase in sections to design a device to eliminate inrush current

articleTitle: EM Environmental Evaluation of HVDC Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Summary form only given. The effects of corona space charge arising from HVDC transmission lines are much more significant than that in AC transmission lines due to the extended distribution of the DC space charge. The space charge greatly influences the audible noise, radio interference, and the electric field strength on the ground and in space, which are very important environmental considerations for HVDC transmission lines. Therefore, line designers must predict the audio noise (AN), radio interference (RI) and the electric field strength around HVDC transmission lines. A convenient, powerful computer program called "SESEnviroPlus" has been developed to fulfil the need for such calculations. Complete description of RI and AN performance of a transmission line generally involve three characteristics, which are discussed in this paper

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Fields, Safety and Health
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Handling electric equipment may cause currents in the body and the methods and measures to protect people are accepted worldwide. However, the safety and health when exposed to electromagnetic fields which cause also currents in the body, is controversial. The actual guidelines and standards are using safety factors (SF) to protect people. To cope with controversial problems and stochastic effects such as long term effects and the precautionary principle, we propose the introduction of a health factor (HF)

articleTitle: Harmful electromagnetic effect on affected line from disturbing line
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: When two transmission lines are parallel, one line will disturb another due to inductive and capacitive coupling. This paper presents precise formulas for calculating interference in symbolic form. It illustrates relationship between interference and mutual inductance, capacitance, impedance, attenuation, parallel length clearly. Some new work has been done. One most common situation is considered, in which two lines parallel have attenuation and their length are not equal. In addition, some important cases are used to verify the solution

articleTitle: A Digital Filtering Method to Process the Convolution in FDTD Analysis of Transmission Line Equations
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Aimed to solve the time-domain convolution in the analysis of transmission line coupling problems, a digital filtering method is proposed to be used in the one-dimensional FDTD computations. Discrete transfer function that represents features of ground impedance is applied to simplify the convolution. Examples demonstrate that the method is effective when the conductivity of the soil is between 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>S/m and 10<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sub>S/m . Algorithms for the combination of digital filtering with FDTD are presented. This digital filtering method can save both the computation time and reduce the memory cost in calculation

articleTitle: The Electro-magnetic Environment of Standard Frequency and Time Signal Emission in Japan
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The observations of electro-magnetic environment in the LF band performed in 2004. The results show the possibility that radio control clocks miss time signals emitted at 40 kHz and 60 kHz. An example of noise source, stray emission from electric instruments, is also reported

Author Keywords: standard frequency and time signal emission

articleTitle: Effects of Erythrocyte Relative Chemo-luminescence Intensities Induced by H2O2 in Mice Exposed to EMP
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The changes of erythrocyte chemo-luminescence intensity induced by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> in mice exposed to the different field intensity of nuclear electromagnetic pulse (EMP) are examined. Using chemo-luminescence induced by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to investigate the changes of luminescence intensity of the erythrocyte in mice under the EMP radiation. The higher the concentration of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sub>, the greater the luminescence intensity of erythrocyte in mice (P<0.01), and the concentration of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is the best at the 4.8 mmol/L. The luminescence intensity of erythrocyte in mice increased as 1.32 times with the normal control at the 0.5 h after 400 kVmiddotm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> EMP irradiation. With the time after irradiation extending, the luminescence intensity decreased gradually to reach below the control at 12 h and 24 h (P<0.05); the luminescence intensity of 100 kVmiddotm<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sub> and 200 kVmiddotm-1EMP decreased significantly to be 50% of the control at 6 h and recovered at 12 h, but the luminescence intensity of 200 kVmiddotm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> EMP increased significantly at 24 h (P<0.01). The luminescence intensity of erythrocyte increased induced by H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> after the high field intensity of EMP irradiation, and it decreased after the moderately field intensity irradiation, and it didn't change almost after the low field EMP irradiation. The relative luminescence intensities changed greatly with the field intensity and the time following the EMP irradiation

articleTitle: High Frequency Conducted Disturbance Analysis of Driving System in Fuel Cell Vehicle
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Hybrid electric vehicle has serious EMC problems. In this paper, with modeling of driving system, the conducted electromagnetic disturbance is analyzed. The parameters are obtained by experiments of system impedance. Affections to the noise patterns caused by major parameters in the model are compared

articleTitle: Effects of position uncertainties on the null width and depth of an adaptive array with subarrays
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: It is often desirable to widen the interference null width in an adapted pattern to impart robustness into the realized adapted array in some real environments. Position errors affect the null width and depth of an adaptive array with subarrays. This paper analyzes the effects of position errors on the null width and depth of an adaptive array with subarrays. The expressions between element position error, subarray position error and the covariance matrix of the input signals are derived. Computer simulation illustrates the effects of position errors on the null width and depth of an adaptive array with subarrays

articleTitle: Anisotropy & polarization analysis in a cubic mode-stirred chamber
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Summary form only given. Anisotropy and polarization are two important aspects of stochastic field generation in reverberation chambers. Yet they are seldom directly measured but rather indirectly demonstrated from field homogeneity and CDF validation. In this paper, anisotropy and random polarization are experimentally addressed in a small cubic mode stirred chamber by means of field anisotropy and cross-correlation coefficients. Those are directly calculated from field component measurements carried out in the frequency band of 900 MHz - 2.5 GHz by means of a broadband triaxial E-field probe. The effect of cavity wall proximity on polarization is also demonstrated

articleTitle: On Electric Potential Fix-point of Grounding for Isotropic Electromagnetic Shield Enclosure
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: The norm of d'Alembertian for the time harmonic electromagnetic field is analysed by introducing matrix operator f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and gage functions in Minkowski space. Furthermore, the electric potential fix-point of electric potential sequence of the grounded shield enclosure is investigated by applying with lowest energy principle and Banach compression mapping theorem. It is verified the zero electric potential is the fix-point of grounded shield electric potential sequence

articleTitle: A Design of AWG Based on DDS Using the SOPC Technique
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a design of AWG based on DDS and SOPC technique. The DDS's spurious noise and several improving method are discussed. The realization of the DDS with FM and PM on FPGA is detailed. The software development for AWG based on NiosII and the design of analog circuit for signal's output are introduced. The testing result is satisfying

articleTitle: Analyzing the Scattering Near-Field from Complex Targets
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a theory method to calculate and analyze the scattering near field from some simple and complex targets, using high-frequency approximation. By calculating the near-field RCS of some simple and complex targets based on the SCTE (scattering from complex targets and environments) system, the results show that there are much difference between the near field and the far field. And the characteristics of the near field are more complicated. This method has practical engineering value in the area of the electromagnetic interference (EMI) prediction and electromagnetic scattering (EMS) et al

articleTitle: Time-domain Reconstruction of a Two-dimensional Dielectric Cylinder by Using Real-coded Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Time-domain reconstruction of a two-dimensional dielectric cylinder by using real-coded genetic algorithm is presented in this paper. Scattering from the dielectric cylinder is solved by using finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD). The dielectric cylinder is represented by a set of geometrical and constitutive parameters. The electromagnetic inverse scattering problem is to retrieve these parameters given the measured time-domain scattered electric fields on finite receivers. It is cast into an optimization problem by defining the objective function as the relative error between the measured and simulated time-domain scattered electric fields on finite receivers. The optimization problem is then solved by using the real-coded genetic algorithm. Good agreement is observed between true profiles and numerically reconstructed ones

articleTitle: A Novel Array Pattern Synthesis Approach Based on Inagaki Modes
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel approach to arbitrary array pattern synthesis utilizing Inagaki modes in a least mean square sense is presented in this paper. The algorithm, involving arrays with arbitrary geometry and incorporating mutual coupling effect, can accurately determine element excitations required to yield desired field pattern. The orthogonality of the Inagaki modes is used to ensure the agreement between the desired and computed patterns. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated with a numerical example

articleTitle: EMC Design of 10kW DC Switch Power Supply
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a design of the 10 kW DC switch power supply to meet the corresponding EMC demand. The 12-pulse rectifier and a novel PSFB ZVS PWM technology are proposed to reduce conduction interference and dv/dt (di/dt) of the main circuit. Some necessary methods are adopted in schematic diagram design, PCB layout, high frequency transformer technics and structure design. All these measures, tested by EMI experiment, are valid

articleTitle: Effect of EMP on mice polydactylia and related genes expression (Gli3, Shh and Fgf4) during the development of mice limbs
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper observe mice polydactylia induced by EMP and related genes expressions (GliS5 Shh and Fgf4) during the development of mice limbs. Mature female mice were mated overnight with male mice (2:1). The morning on which a vaginal plug was found was designated as fetation-day-0. The pregnant mice were randomly divided into control group and EMP radiation group. Mice in the EMP radiation group were exposed to EMP from fetation-day-7 to fetation-day-10. The field intensity was 400 kVmiddotm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with 400 pulses. On the fetation-day-18, the embryos were taken out by cesarean section. The polydactylia were recorded. Morphological analysis of polydactylia was performed by using Alcian blue-Alizarin red staining method. The pregnant mice were randomly divided into negative control group, positive control group and EMP radiation group. Mice in the EMP radiation group were exposed to EMP from fetation-day-7 to fetation-day-10. The field intensity was 400 kVmiddotm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> with 400 pulses.
