The proliferation index and differentiation index of control group are lower than that of EMP-treated group. EMP exposure may influence the proliferation and differentiation of mouse embryonic limb bud cells

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation of UWB Propagation in Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, an efficient ray tracing model is developed for ultra wideband (UWB) indoor environments. The ray tracing model is founded and used to simulate the propagation environment of a typical office. A time domain approach is used to determine all propagation paths. The time and spatial properties of the UWB channel are presented well by using ray tracing, which include RMS, distribution of ray energy and channel impulse response. Hence, the model is suitable to rapidly evaluate UWB channel characteristics in indoor environments with different input signals

articleTitle: The Damage Voltage Calculation of ESD based on Damage Parameters of Square wave
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In the short pulse region, the knot surface breakdown is the chief damage that was induced by the electromagnetic pulse to the electronic devices. The power that leads the devices damaged relates with the pulse width. Electrostatic discharge (ESD) is a course with high electric potential and instantaneous large current, and ESD breakdown of the electronic devices is quite similar with it. According to the Wunch-Bell's model theory that appraises pulse width threshold of semiconductor device, combining the human-body model (HBM) of ESD, the theoretical formula calculating damage threshold voltage of ESD was derivated. It provides one kind of method to estimate ESD damage threshold in the condition of lacked experimental data

articleTitle: The Research of Testing Technology of High Power Electromagnetic Pulses in Exploding Environment
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, a simple electromagnetic test technology which can be applied to test transient pulses is introduced. The system are composed of Rogowski coil, external integrator, multistage resistance voltage divider, integraph A/D, data processing system, trigger and computer. The theory of Rogowski coil is briefly described. The structure of measuring system and the measurement result are presented in this paper

articleTitle: Investigation of 2-layer Shield for Magnetic Shielding Considering Magnetic Hysteresis
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the study of 2-layer shielding against power frequency magnetic field in order to increase the shielding effectiveness of the shield. The work has been investigated by finite element method (FEM) considering the hysteresis effect of magnetic materials. The investigations show that the shielding effectiveness of the shield is affected by several factors: the nonlinear property of materials, order of materials, spacing between layers, etc

articleTitle: Study of EMI Signal Feature Extraction Based on Wavelet Packet
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A wavelet packet technique to extract feature of electromagnetic interferences (EMI) signals in power electronic devices is presented. This method can be used to analyze the signals with different EMI and to get the interference feature based on its energy from the wavelet packet analysis result. By using the EMI signal singularity property, an improved measure is put forward and their qualities are appraised

articleTitle: A Method of Improving Isolation between Fuselage-mounted Antennas
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Metal scattering body (bodies) mounted around fuselage-mounted antennas to improve isolation is presented in this paper. Metal scattering body (bodies) will disturb radiation patters of airborne antenna, and isolation between fuselage-mounted antennas can be enhanced by choosing structure, size and mounted-location of metal scattering body (bodies) availably. Theoretical analysis and computer emulational results show that the method is proper, doable, and effective. It can solve some engineering problems, such as transmitters interfere with receivers and safety margins are inadequate in complex electromagnetic circumstance

articleTitle: Novel Dual Feed Broadband Antennas with a Combined Shape
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: A small broadband antenna is presented for HF/VHF/UHF communication or EMC. The antenna integrates several techniques such as construction combination, dual feed and matching with sleeves. In a bandwidth greater than 5 octaves, the antenna's VSWR is less than 2.5, with dimensions much smaller than those of the discone or discage antennas

articleTitle: Novel Temporal Basis Functions for Time Domain Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: In the paper, a novel scheme is presented to construct the temporal basis functions for time domain electric field integral equation (TD-EFIE). An optimal algorithm is developed to find the optimum temporal basis functions, which are used to stabilize the marching-on-in-time (MOT) process. The proposed temporal basis functions possess the advantage of poor high-frequency content in spectral and any-order continuous derivative in shape. Therefore, they can provide much more stable explicit MOT solution. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed temporal basis functions

Author Keywords: time domain electric field integral equation (TD-EFIE)

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Pulses Induced Fluctuation in arterial pressures without changes in the heart rate in Rats
publicationTitle: The 2006 4th Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics
abstract: Functional indices of the cardiovascular system (heart rate, systolic, mean, and diastolic pressures) were selected to represent biological end points that may be susceptible to the EMP exposure. Male SD rats were subjected to sham exposure, 200 kV/m (0.5pps, 200 pulses altogether, SAR=50mW/kg) or 400 kV/m (0.5pps, 200 pulses altogether, SAR=75mW/kg) EMP fields in a tapered parallel plate GTEM cell. Cardiovascular functions were evaluated from instant to 4 weeks after exposures using a noninvasive tail-cuff photoelectric sensor sphygmomanometer. Significant up and down fluctuation of the arterial blood pressure was found. In contrast, heart rate was not altered by these exposures.
